description: Composite figure mixing two TEM bright-field micrographs, three indexed selected-area diffraction (SAED) patterns and three colour-coded phase maps, all concerning a ferrite-based low-density steel warm-deformed in compression. (a) TEM bright-field image of ferrite (black dot labelled "F") after deformation to interrupted strain 0.3 at 500 °C, 500 nm scale bar; white arrows mark HDDWs and "Tangled Dislocations", and red dashed lines mark "Primary" and "Secondary" slip traces labelled "{110} and {112} Slip Traces" crossing at one point. Immediately below are three SAED patterns with 2 1/nm scale bars: "F ferrite" and "ferrite 1", both Z=[113], with (000), {110} and (2̄11)/(11̄0) reflections, and "austenite 2", Z=[1̄11], with (000), (0̄22), (202), (2̄20) reflections. (b) TEM bright-field image, 1 μm scale bar, with white arrows pointing to fresh ferrite grains inside a parent austenite island and black dots 1 and 2 marking the analysed areas. (c,d) (6 μm scale bar, labels (i),(ii)) and (e) (15 μm scale bar, label (iii)) are phase maps, red = austenite and green = ferrite per the caption, with dashed-black ovals outlining sheared deformation bands, "Austenite Shearing" text and red/green arrows marking austenite and ferrite formation through the bands.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field micrograph of the deformed ferrite phase, 500 nm scale bar, labelled F (black dot). White arrows mark HDDWs (high dislocation density walls) and 'Tangled Dislocations'; red dashed lines mark 'Primary' and 'Secondary' {110} and {112} Slip Traces intersecting at a single point. Strain 0.3 at 500 °C.

Three selected-area diffraction patterns printed under (a), each with a 2 1/nm scale bar. 'F ferrite' and 'ferrite 1' are indexed with Z=[113] (reflections (000), {110}, (2̄11)/(11̄0)); 'austenite 2' is indexed with Z=[1̄11] showing (000), (0̄22), (202), (2̄20).

TEM bright-field micrograph, 1 μm scale bar, showing a relatively defect-free grain region inside a heavily deformed parent austenite matrix; white arrows point to fresh ferrite grains, and black dots 1 and 2 mark where the ferrite and austenite diffraction patterns were taken.

Colour phase map labelled (i), 6 μm scale bar, red and green phases with dashed-black ovals tracing sheared deformation bands and red/green arrows; the text 'Austenite Shearing' appears top-left. Red = austenite, green = ferrite per caption.

Colour phase map labelled (ii), 6 μm scale bar, same red/green colour scheme; a large red (austenite) region sheared by dashed-black-oval deformation bands with green (ferrite) stringers along the bands; 'Austenite Shearing' text at right.

Colour phase map labelled (iii), 15 μm scale bar, lower magnification view with large red (austenite) and green (ferrite) regions and fine red decoration along boundaries; no arrows or dashed ovals drawn.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field micrograph with a 500 nm scale bar showing the ferrite phase (black dot labelled 'F') containing tangled dislocations and high dislocation density walls (HDDWs), with red dashed lines marking 'Primary' and 'Secondary' slip traces labelled '{110} and {112} Slip Traces'.

Three SAED patterns are printed beneath panel (a), each carrying a 2 1/nm scale bar: 'F ferrite' and 'ferrite 1' are indexed with zone axis Z=[113] (BCC ferrite), while 'austenite 2' is indexed with Z=[1̄11] (FCC austenite).

Panel (b) is a TEM bright-field micrograph with a 1 μm scale bar in which white arrows point to fresh ferrite grains formed within a parent austenite island, and black dots labelled 1 and 2 mark the two areas analysed by diffraction.

Panels (c), (d) and (e) are colour-coded phase maps with 6 μm, 6 μm and 15 μm scale bars and corner labels (i), (ii) and (iii); dashed-black ovals outline deformation bands, and (c) and (d) carry the text 'Austenite Shearing'.

The caption states that red and green arrows in the phase maps indicate austenite and ferrite formation through deformation bands, respectively, and that these panels are higher magnifications of selected areas in Fig. 2a and b.

The caption states the microstructures were examined at an interrupted strain of 0.3 and 500 °C, with (a) showing dislocation configuration and multiple slip traces within the ferrite and (b) formation of fresh ferrite grains within parent austenite islands.
The citing text reports that at interrupted strain 0.3 many dislocations were tangled to form cell structures within the ferrite and a planar slip-like character started to form.

The citing text states that strain within the ferrite is mainly accommodated by activation of multiple slip systems {110}<111> and {112}<111>, making formation and intersection of slip bands highly probable.

The citing text states that panels (c) and (d) are higher-magnification views of material compressed at 500 °C to a true strain of 0.6, where deformation-induced 'ferrite to austenite' (DIAT) and 'austenite to ferrite' (DIFT) transformations occur simultaneously along deformation bands.

The citing text states that such transformation-based strain accommodation cannot be characterized in microstructures deformed at the higher temperature of 600 °C, referring to panel (e) — so (e) is the 600 °C comparison rather than a 500 °C result.
The citing text attributes the observed flow softening at the low temperature regime (Fig. 1c) to strain-induced austenite-to-ferrite transformation acting as a strain compensation mechanism.
No colour-scale legend is printed on the phase maps themselves; the assignment red = austenite and green = ferrite is asserted only by the caption, and the maps contain no numeric phase fractions.
